newsitem.title: CANADA: Air France to move Montreal cargo handling.
newsitem.headline: Air France to move Montreal cargo handling.

text.p: Air France said it will move ts cargo-handling to Dorval Airport once passenger flights begin using the airport in May.

The carrier's four weekly freighters will continue to land at Mirabel Airport, north of the city, and freight will be trucked to Dorval through an arrangement with the local airport authority, the airline added.

Sixty percent of Air France's cargo traffic is bellyhold freight moving in passenger or combi (combination cargo/passenger) aircraft. These aircraft will land at Dorval, part of a shift of international passenger services from Mirabel to Dorval, which served as Montreal's international airport until Mirabel was opened in 1975.
Air France Cargo had expressed reservations about the added handling expense incurred by having to put its freighters into Mirabel while its passenger planes used Dorval.

Dorval, much closer to downtown, has continued to handle domestic and Canada-U.S. flights and is more popular with travellers living in the western, eastern and southern districts and periphery of the greater Montreal area.
While agreeing the shift of international passenger flights to Dorval, the airport authority decided that all freighter flights, as well as passenger charters, will continue to use Mirabel.

The authority is planning a two-tiered fee structure making it cheaper for carriers to stay at Mirabel if they choose, but most scheduled airlines are expected to choose Dorval for competitive reasons.

Air Canada, Canadian Airlines International and Israel's El Al EL AL.CN among others have said they will move their international flights to Dorval. British Airways, a marketing partner of CAI, is expected to follow suit, as is Swissair, a marketing partner of Air Canada. -Air Cargo Newsroom Tel +44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
